prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: One reviewer who knew the original text well wrote that the production had ______ the play.

worlds.passage: In 1931 a touring company staged a new version of a little-known seventeenth-century tragedy in which a queen gives up the soldier she loves and dies of grief. Its director wanted audiences to watch the love affair begin and end, so he wrote a scene of the couple's first meeting to open the evening and a scene at the queen's tomb to close it, with the old text kept whole between them. Patrons who had booked late suppers found the restaurants shut, though most admitted the queen's last speech had left them in tears. One reviewer who knew the original text well wrote that the production had ______ the play.
worlds.explanation: New scenes framed the whole old text, and patrons found the restaurants shut, so the production "lengthened" the play. "Jumbled" fails because the old text sat intact between the new opening and closing scenes; "gutted" fails because that text was kept whole; "lampooned" fails because the queen's last speech left audiences in tears.

jumbled.why: the original ran intact, in sequence, between the added frames

gutted.why: nothing was cut, so the play's core survived

lampooned.why: a production that moves audiences to tears is not mocking the play

worlds.passage: In 1931 a touring company staged a new version of a little-known seventeenth-century tragedy in which a queen gives up the soldier she loves and dies of grief. Its director thought suspense cheapened tragedy, so he opened on the queen's deathbed and let each later scene show an earlier stage of the affair, ending with the lovers' first meeting. Since every speech the author wrote was still there, merely displaced, the evening ran its usual three hours, yet the lobby afterward held more puzzlement than weeping, as patrons argued over who the soldier was. One reviewer who knew the original text well wrote that the production had ______ the play.
worlds.explanation: Running the scenes backward left audiences arguing over the basic story, so the production "jumbled" the play. "Lengthened" fails because the evening ran its usual three hours; "gutted" fails because every speech was still there, merely displaced; "lampooned" fails because the reaction was puzzlement in place of the weeping intended, not laughter.

lengthened.why: the running time did not grow

lampooned.why: audiences were confused by a serious production, not laughing at a mocking one

worlds.passage: In 1931 a touring company staged a new version of a little-known seventeenth-century tragedy in which a queen gives up the soldier she loves and dies of grief. Its director found the queen's long speeches of doubt slow, and he struck them, though they are the only place where she weighs her throne against her love. What remained, played in the author's sequence, was a brisk run of duels and deaths, and patrons were out in good time for supper, dry-eyed and unable to say why the queen had died. One reviewer who knew the original text well wrote that the production had ______ the play.
worlds.explanation: Striking the only speeches in which the queen weighs her choice left audiences "unable to say why the queen had died," so the production "gutted" the play. "Lengthened" fails because patrons were out in good time for supper; "jumbled" fails because the scenes kept the author's sequence; "lampooned" fails because the audience left puzzled, not amused.

lengthened.quote: out in good time for supper

lampooned.quote: unable to say why the queen had died
lampooned.why: the effect was confusion about motive, not ridicule

worlds.passage: In 1931 a touring company staged a new version of a little-known seventeenth-century tragedy in which a queen gives up the soldier she loves and dies of grief. Its director found the old verse stiff, so he had his actors recite every line of it in a quavering singsong and swoon at each exit. The queen's death, which still ends the evening as the author intended, drew the loudest laughter of the night, and patrons were out in good time for an early supper. One reviewer who knew the original text well wrote that the production had ______ the play.
worlds.explanation: Singsong delivery and swooning made the queen's death the night's biggest laugh, so the production "lampooned" the play. "Lengthened" fails because patrons were out in time for an early supper; "jumbled" fails because the death still ends the evening as the author intended; "gutted" fails because every line was recited, so nothing was cut away.

lengthened.quote: in good time for an early supper
lengthened.why: the evening did not run long

jumbled.quote: still ends the evening as the author intended

gutted.why: the text was complete; only its delivery mocked it
